Bench: Vishal Mishra  NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:70520  1   IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT JABALPUR  BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE VISHAL MISHRA  ON THE 6 th OF OCTOBER, 2025  WRIT PETITION No. 14561 of 2010  SMT. YASHODA BAI AND OTHERS  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH AND OTHERS  Appearance:
 Shri Prakash Upadhyay - Senior Advocate with Shri S  Advocate for the petitioners.
 Shri Abhishek Singh - Govt. Advocate for respondent  ORDER

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The present petition has been filed assailing the order dated 21.07.2010 passed by the respondent No.2/Additional Collector-cum- Competent Authority (under the Urban Land Ceiling and Regulation Act, Jabalpur), whereby the application filed by the petitioner Smt. Yashoda Bai in pursuance to the order passed by this Court in WP No. 8012 of 2005 dated 16.08.2005 has been rejected.
2.

entities.text: Urban Land Ceiling and Regulation Act, Jabalpur
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is a case of the petitioner that Chandrika Prasad was original owner of the land and was in possession thereof bearing Khasra No.222 admeasuring 4.087 hectares and Khasra No.228/3 admeasuring 1.802 hectares situated at Village Kathonda and Khasra No.60 admeasuring 0.190 hectare situated at Village Amkhera Tehsil and District Jabalpur.

Chandrika Prasad filed a return under Section 6 of the Urban Land (Ceiling and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:70520 2 WP-14561-2010 Regulation) Act, 1976 (hereinafter referred to as 'Act of 1976') and the case was registered as Case No. 51A/90(B-9)/81-82.

entities.text: Urban Land (Ceiling and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:70520 2 WP-14561-2010 Regulation) Act, 1976
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: In that case, the competent authority declared 59366.20 sq. m. of land as surplus.
A draft statement under Section 8(1) of the Act of 1976 was issued.
Thereafter, under Section 9 thereof, the final statement was prepared.
A notification in terms of Section 10(1) thereof was published on 01.03.1985 and a notification under Section 10(3) of the Act of 1976 was published in the Madhya Pradesh Gazette on 08.01.1993.

Thereafter, a notice was issued Smt. Yashoda Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19492742/
1 to Chandrika Prasad under Section 10(5) of the Act of 1976 and he was asked to surrender the surplus land to the State Government which was served on 04.11.1993 and thereafter, vide possession letter dated 31.01.1994, Tahsildar (Nazul) has taken possession of the land in question and the land is recorded in the name of the State Government.

entities.text: Smt. Yashoda Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. The Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976 was repealed by the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Repeal Act, 1999.

entities.text: Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Repeal Act, 1999
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Thereafter, the petitioners filed an application under Section 4 of the Repeal Act of 1999 alleging that they are legal heirs of Chandrika Prasad and are still in possession of the property in question.
The possession of the land was never taken by the State Government or any competent authority.
The said application was rejected on 18.01.2005 which was put to challenge by filing a Writ Petition No. 8012 of 2005.

The said writ petition was allowed and order dated 18.01.2005 was set aside and the direction was issued to respondent No. 2 to make proper inquiry and give full opportunity of hearing to the petitioner and thereafter decide the case on merits whether the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:70520 3 WP-14561-2010 possession of the land was taken in accordance with law or not.

Thereafter, vide impugned order dated 21.07.2010, the application filed by the petitioner was again rejected pointing out the fact that the Tahsildar has taken possession of the vacant land in accordance with Section 10(6) of Act of 1976.
4.
Challenge is made to the impugned order on the ground that the notice under Section 10(5) of Act of 1976 was never received by Chandrika Prasad.
It is nowhere mentioned that the notice was served on holder on 04.11.1993 and despite receiving the notice, he has not appeared nor filed any objection.
No opportunity was granted to Chandrika Prasad to surrender the surplus land and to keep the land of his choice in his own possession which is the basic requirement of Section 10 of the Act of 1976.
Therefore, the entire proceedings are per se illegal.
5. It is submitted that as the petitioners are still in possession of the land in question, by introduction of the Repeal Act of 1999, the entire ceiling proceedings have come to an end.

In fact,
the entire land has to be reverted back to the petitioners who are legal heirs of Chandrika Prasad.

In support of the arguments, petitioners' counsel has relied upon the judgments passed in the cases of Veer Narayan Rathore vs State of M.P. and others reported in (2015) 4 MP LJ 656, Gajanan Kamlya Patil v. Addl. Collector & Competent Authority reported in (2014) 12 SCC 523 and A.P. Electrical Equipment Corporation vs Tahsildar and Others reported in 2025 SCC OnLine SC 447.

6. On notice being issued, a reply has been filed by the respondents NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:70520 4 WP-14561-2010 denying the petition averments.

Apart from the factual position, it is contended that this petition has been filed through general power of attorney which itself is not maintainable as the general power of attorney is not an authenticated document in view of Section 33 of the Registration Act, 1908.
It is also insufficiently stamped.

It is further contended that the petitioner has suppressed the material information from this Court; a Civil Suit No.46A of 2008 was filed by Smt. Bhavana Patel wherein Rajesh Patel, Smt. Ramvati, Smt. Yashoda Bai and Rakesh Kumar were arrayed as defendants.
It was filed on 04.11.2004.

They prayed for declaration that the agreement of sale dated 10.10.2003 executed by the defendants No.1 and 2 in favour of Smt. Yashoda Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19492742/
2 defendants No. 3 and 4 as well as general power of attorney dated 03.09.2003 be declared as void and ineffective being obtained by playing fraud.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Another Civil Suit No. 29A of 2004 was filed by Rajesh Patel and Smt. Ramvati which was dismissed on 01.04.2004 by Thirteenth Civil Judge Class II Jabalpur against which a Misc. Civil Appeal No. 1 of 2005 was filed which was dismissed on 04.03.2005 and the order has attained finality.

entities.text: Thirteenth Civil Judge Class II Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The petitioners have also filed a Civil Suit No. 3A of 2004 before Eighth Civil Judge Class II Jabalpur for declaration and permanent injunction challenging agreement for sale dated 03.05.2002 and 17.01.2003 which was dismissed vide order dated 18.09.2006 which was put to challenge in Misc. Civil Appeal No.15 of 2007 and the same was also dismissed by Eighth Additional Judge to the Court of District Judge by order dated 31.07.2007,
against which a Civil Revision No.382 of 2007 was filed which was dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 08.05.2009 with liberty to file a writ petition under NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:70520 5 WP-14561-2010 Article 227 of the Constitution of India.

entities.text: Eighth Civil Judge Class II Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The said order has attained finality.
7. It is submitted that the relief which has been sought in the present petition if granted will adversely affect the civil proceedings.

The order declaring the vacant land in excess of ceiling limits dated 22.03.1994 passed by the competent authority in Case No.51/A-90-B-9/81-82 was assailed by filing an appeal before the Commissioner Jabalpur Division Jabalpur being Appeal No.
75/5-90-B-9/1998-1999 and the said appeal was dismissed on 15.04.1999 as time barred.
The same has attained finality as there was no challenge to the said order.
The possession of the land has already been taken by the authorities in the year 1993.
Thereafter, Smt. Ramvati Bai and Rajesh Patel encroached upon the land in question and started cultivation.

The Tahsildar on an application filed by Shankarlal Patel for removal of encroachment has passed an order on 07.03.2011 holding that Smt. Ramvati Bai and Rajesh Patel failed to prove their title over the land in question.
It is submitted that the said order has not put to challenge at any point of time and the same also attained finality.

As far as the ground raised by the petitioner that the proceedings under Section 10(5) of the Act of 1976 were never taken up by the authorities is concerned, it is contended that proper notices were served to Chandrika Prasad with respect to the surplus land and only thereafter,
the possession was taken and the land was recorded in the name of the State Government.
The State counsel has produced the original records to demonstrate the same.

It is argued that once the possession of the land has been taken up and the land has been recorded in the name of State Government coupled with the fact that no proceedings were initiated by NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:70520 6 WP-14561-2010 Chandrika Prasad at the relevant time in view of the Repeal Act of 1999, then the possession of a person would be that of an encroacher only and he cannot claim adverse possession.
Such person cannot be treated as a person in rightful possession.
Further, the application was filed by the daughter of Chandrika Prasad which was rejected by the respondents-authorities.

8. Counsel appearing for the respondents/State has relied upon the judgment passed by the coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Vijay Ram vs State of M.P. and others : Writ Petition No.255 of 2006 (Gwalior Bench) decided on 27.02.2025 wherein detailed consideration regarding vesting of the land in the Government was taken note of as well as in the case of Kishan Lal and others vs Municipal Corporation Bhopal and others :

On these grounds, he has prayed for dismissal of the writ petition.

9. Heard learned counsels for the parties and perused the records.
10.
It is not disputed that 59366.20 sq. m. of land which belonged to Chandrika Prasad was declared surplus.
The draft statement under Section 8(1) of the Act of 1976 was prepared and thereafter final statement under Section 9 thereof was issued.
The notification was published in the Madhya Pradesh Gazette and a notification under Section 10(3) was also issued on 08.01.1993.

The respondents have issued notice under Section 10(5) to Chandrika Prasad on 28.10.1993 directing him to surrender the excess land within 30 days failing which proceedings under Section 10(6) of the Act of 1976 would be initiated for taking forceful possession.
Thereafter, the possession of land was taken on 31.01.1994 in ex parte proceedings.

After NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:70520 7 WP-14561-2010 taking of the possession by the State Government, the land was recorded in the name of State Government.
This goes to show that the land vested in the State Government.

There is no challenge by Chandrika Prasad to the proceedings under Sections 10(5) and 10(6) of the Act of 1976 for taking possession of the land in question and thereafter the proceedings were initiated by the daughter of Chandrika Prasad under the provisions of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Repeal Act, 1999 on the ground that the possession of land was never taken and she is still in possession of the land in question.

entities.text: Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Repeal Act, 1999
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: However, the fact remains that they were declared encroachers of the property in question by the Court of Tahsildar.
Series of civil litigations was filed by the parties seeking title over the land in question but they remained unsuccessful before any of the forum.
The petitioner preferred a writ petition before this Court which was disposed of in the year 2005 directing the authorities to reconsider the application filed by daughter of Chandrika Prasad.
11. On perusal of the record, it is reflected that the notice was served upon Chandrika Prasad on 04.11.1993 but despite service of notice, he has chosen not to surrender the land in question.
The record further indicates that Chandrika Prasad initiated proceedings before the Commissioner Jabalpur Division Jabalpur for declaring the order that declared the land to be surplus as illegal.
The appeal preferred by Chandrika Prasad through legal heirs was dismissed vide order dated 15.04.1999 and the same has attained finality.

12. Regarding vesting of the land in the State Government, the coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Kishan Lal and others (supra) has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:70520 8 WP-14561-2010 observed as under :
15.
Thus, it is clear that once, the land has vested in the State Govt., then it cannot be returned back by denotifying from the acquisition.
Once the land is acquired, it vests in the State free from all encumbrances.
The land owner becomes persona non grata once the land vests in the State.
He has a right to get compensation only for the same.

The person interested cannot claim the right of restoration of land on any ground,
whatsoever.

Once the land has vested in the State Govt., then there cannot be any rider on the right Smt. Yashoda Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19492742/
4 of the State Govt. to change land use.

entities.text: Yashoda Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. In the present case, once the entire proceedings were carried out in accordance with law and the possession of land was taken by the respondents-authorities and the land vested in the State Government coupled with the fact that the order declaring the petitioner to be encroacher on the land in question was passed by the Tahsildar in the year 2011 itself and the fact that the factum of series of civil litigations initiated by the parties is suppressed from this Court wherein some of the parties have even lost their claims in civil proceedings upto the appellate stage and those proceedings have attained finality, no relief can be extended to the petitioners.
The proceedings under the Act of 1976 were rightly conducted by the respondents-authorities.
Hence, no interference is called for.
14. The petition sans merit and is accordingly dismissed.
No order as to costs.
Let original record be returned to State counsel.

(VISHAL MISHRA) JUDGE VV Smt. Yashoda Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19492742/
